passages.text: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel, they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the families, saying, “Let us build with you because, like you, we seek your God and have been sacrificing to Him since the time of King Esar-haddon of Assyria, who brought us here.”
passages.sermon:
The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard news.
They heard that the exiles were building a temple.
The temple was for the LORD, the God of Israel.
These enemies went to Zerubbabel.
They also went to the heads of the families.
They spoke to them.
They said, “Let us build with you.”
They said, “We seek your God as you do.”
They said, “We have been sacrificing to Him.”
They said, “We have done this since the days of King Esar-haddon of Assyria.”
They said, “He brought us here.”
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ צָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּֽי־ בְנֵ֤י הַגּוֹלָה֙ בּוֹנִ֣ים הֵיכָ֔ל לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ אֶל־ זְרֻבָּבֶ֜ל וְאֶל־ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽאָב֗וֹת וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נִבְנֶ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֔ם כִּ֣י כָכֶ֔ם נִדְר֖וֹשׁ לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹא אֲנַ֣חְנוּ זֹבְחִ֗ים מִימֵי֙ אֵסַ֤ר חַדֹּן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר הַמַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖נוּ פֹּֽה׃

passages.text: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other heads of the families of Israel replied, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God, since we alone must build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as Cyrus king of Persia has commanded us.”
passages.sermon:
Zerubbabel was a leader of the Israelites.
Jeshua was also a leader of the Israelites.
The other heads of the families of Israel were with them.
They spoke to the people who wanted to help build the temple.
They said, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God.”
They said, “We alone must build it for the LORD, the God of Israel.”
They said, “Cyrus, king of Persia, has commanded us to do this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָהֶ֨ם זְרֻבָּבֶ֜ל וְיֵשׁ֗וּעַ וּשְׁאָ֨ר רָאשֵׁ֤י הָֽאָבוֹת֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־ לָ֣כֶם וָלָ֔נוּ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ כִּי֩ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ יַ֜חַד נִבְנֶ֗ה לַֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔נוּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־ פָּרָֽס׃

passages.text: Then the people of the land set out to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to build.
passages.sermon: The people of the land lived in the area around Judah.\r\nThey tried to discourage the people of Judah.\r\nThey made the people of Judah afraid to build.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ עַם־ הָאָ֔רֶץ מְרַפִּ֖ים יְדֵ֣י עַם־ יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמְבַלַהִים אוֹתָ֖ם לִבְנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and down to the reign of Darius king of Persia.
passages.sermon:
The enemies of the people of Judah acted against them.
These enemies hired counselors.
The counselors worked to frustrate the plans of the people of Judah.
This opposition lasted during the reign of Cyrus, king of Persia.
The opposition continued until the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
passages.original: וְסֹכְרִ֧ים עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹעֲצִ֖ים לְהָפֵ֣ר עֲצָתָ֑ם כָּל־ יְמֵ֗י כּ֚וֹרֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס וְעַד־ מַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־ פָּרָֽס׃

passages.text: At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, an accusation was lodged against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Xerxes became king.
This was the beginning of his reign.
People made an accusation.
They accused the people of Judah.
They also accused the people of Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּבְמַלְכוּת֙ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת מַלְכוּת֑וֹ כָּתְב֣וּ שִׂטְנָ֔ה עַל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: And in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his associates wrote a letter to Artaxerxes. It was written in Aramaic and then translated.
passages.sermon:
Artaxerxes was king of Persia.
Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their associates lived during his reign.
They wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes.
They wrote the letter in Aramaic.
They translated the letter into Aramaic.
passages.original: וּבִימֵ֣י אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֗שְׂתָּא כָּתַ֨ב בִּשְׁלָ֜ם מִתְרְדָ֤ת טָֽבְאֵל֙ וּשְׁאָ֣ר כְּנָוֹתוֹ עַל־ אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׂתָּא מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרָ֑ס וּכְתָב֙ הַֽנִּשְׁתְּוָ֔ן כָּת֥וּב אֲרָמִ֖ית וּמְתֻרְגָּ֥ם אֲרָמִֽית׃פ

passages.text: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote the letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows: From Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges and officials over Tripolis, Persia, Erech and Babylon, the Elamites of Susa, and the rest of the peoples whom the great and honorable Ashurbanipal deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and elsewhere west of the Euphrates.
passages.sermon:
Rehum was the commander.
Shimshai was the scribe.
Rehum and Shimshai wrote a letter.
They wrote this letter against Jerusalem.
They sent the letter to King Artaxerxes.
The letter was from Rehum the commander.
It was also from Shimshai the scribe.
It was from their other associates too.
Their associates included judges and officials.
These judges and officials ruled over Tripolis, Persia, Erech, and Babylon.
Some associates were Elamites from Susa.
Other associates were people whom Ashurbanipal deported.
Ashurbanipal was a great and honorable king.
He settled these people in the cities of Samaria.
He also settled them in other places west of the Euphrates River.
passages.original: רְח֣וּם בְּעֵל־ טְעֵ֗ם וְשִׁמְשַׁי֙ סָֽפְרָ֔א כְּתַ֛בוּ אִגְּרָ֥ה חֲדָ֖ה עַל־ יְרוּשְׁלֶ֑ם לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥שְׂתְּא מַלְכָּ֖א כְּנֵֽמָא׃ אֱדַ֜יִן רְח֣וּם בְּעֵל־ טְעֵ֗ם וְשִׁמְשַׁי֙ סָֽפְרָ֔א וּשְׁאָ֖ר כְּנָוָתְה֑וֹן דִּ֠ינָיֵא וַאֲפַרְסַתְכָיֵ֞א טַרְפְּלָיֵ֣א אֲפָֽרְסָיֵ֗א אַרְכְּוָי בָבְלָיֵא֙ שֽׁוּשַׁנְכָיֵ֔א דִּהוּא עֵלְמָיֵֽא׃ וּשְׁאָ֣ר אֻמַּיָּ֗א דִּ֤י הַגְלִי֙ אָסְנַפַּר֙ רַבָּ֣א וְיַקִּירָ֔א וְהוֹתֵ֣ב הִמּ֔וֹ בְּקִרְיָ֖ה דִּ֣י שָׁמְרָ֑יִן וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֲבַֽר־ נַהֲרָ֖ה וּכְעֶֽנֶת׃

passages.text: (This is the text of the letter they sent to him.) To King Artaxerxes, From your servants, the men west of the Euphrates: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came from you to us have returned to Jerusalem. And they are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city, restoring its walls, and repairing its foundations.
passages.sermon:
This is the text of the letter they sent to King Artaxerxes.
The letter is from your servants.
We are the men who live west of the Euphrates River.
Let it be known to the king.
The Jews came from you to us.
They have returned to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is a rebellious and wicked city.
The Jews are rebuilding this city.
They are restoring its walls.
They are repairing its foundations.
passages.original: דְּנָה֙ פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִגַּרְתָּ֔א דִּ֚י שְׁלַ֣חוּ עֲל֔וֹהִי עַל־ אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֖שְׂתְּא מַלְכָּ֑א עַבְדָ֛יךְ אֱנָ֥שׁ עֲבַֽר־ נַהֲרָ֖ה וּכְעֶֽנֶת׃פ יְדִ֙יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֗א דִּ֤י סְלִ֙קוּ֙ מִן־ לְוָתָ֔ךְ עֲלֶ֥ינָא אֲת֖וֹ לִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם קִרְיְתָ֨א מָֽרָדְתָּ֤א וּבִֽאישְׁתָּא֙ בָּנַ֔יִן וְשׁוּרַיָּ אֲשַׁכְלְלוּ וְאֻשַּׁיָּ֖א יַחִֽיטוּ׃

passages.text: Let it now be known to the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, they will not pay tribute, duty, or toll, and the royal treasury will suffer.
passages.sermon:
This letter is addressed to King Artaxerxes.
The letter warns the king about Jerusalem.
The letter says: Let it be known to the king.
If the city of Jerusalem is rebuilt, the people will restore its walls.
If the walls are restored, the people will not pay tribute.
They will not pay duty.
They will not pay toll.
The king’s treasury will lose income.
The royal treasury will suffer.
passages.original: כְּעַ֗ן יְדִ֙יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֠י הֵ֣ן קִרְיְתָ֥א דָךְ֙ תִּתְבְּנֵ֔א וְשׁוּרַיָּ֖ה יִֽשְׁתַּכְלְל֑וּן מִנְדָּֽה־ בְל֤וֹ וַהֲלָךְ֙ לָ֣א יִנְתְּנ֔וּן וְאַפְּתֹ֥ם מַלְכִ֖ים תְּהַנְזִֽק׃

passages.text: Now because we are in the service of the palace and it is not fitting for us to allow the king to be dishonored, we have sent to inform the king that a search should be made of the record books of your fathers. In these books you will discover and verify that the city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, inciting sedition from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.
passages.sermon:
We serve in the king’s palace.
We must not allow the king to be dishonored.
For this reason, we have sent this message to the king.
We inform the king of our concern.
We ask the king to search the record books of his ancestors.
In these books, the king will find the truth about this city.
The records will show that this city is rebellious.
The city has harmed kings and provinces.
The people of this city have caused uprisings since ancient times.
Because of this, the city was destroyed.
passages.original: כְּעַ֗ן כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־ מְלַ֤ח הֵֽיכְלָא֙ מְלַ֔חְנָא וְעַרְוַ֣ת מַלְכָּ֔א לָ֥א אֲ‍ֽרִֽיךְ לַ֖נָא לְמֶֽחֱזֵ֑א עַ֨ל־ דְּנָ֔ה שְׁלַ֖חְנָא וְהוֹדַ֥עְנָא לְמַלְכָּֽא׃ דִּ֡י יְבַקַּר֩ בִּֽסְפַר־ דָּכְרָ֨נַיָּ֜א דִּ֣י אֲבָהָתָ֗ךְ וּ֠תְהַשְׁכַּח בִּסְפַ֣ר דָּכְרָנַיָּא֮ וְתִנְדַּע֒ דִּי֩ קִרְיְתָ֨א דָ֜ךְ קִרְיָ֣א מָֽרָדָ֗א וּֽמְהַנְזְקַ֤ת מַלְכִין֙ וּמְדִנָ֔ן וְאֶשְׁתַּדּוּר֙ עָבְדִ֣ין בְּגַוַּ֔הּ מִן־ יוֹמָ֖ת עָלְמָ֑א עַ֨ל־ דְּנָ֔ה קִרְיְתָ֥א דָ֖ךְ הָֽחָרְבַֽת׃

passages.text: We advise the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are restored, you will have no dominion west of the Euphrates.
passages.sermon:
This message is for the king.
We are the king’s advisors.
We want the king to know something important.
If this city is rebuilt, it will be strong again.
If the walls of this city are restored, it will be protected.
If this happens, the king will lose control west of the Euphrates River.
The king will have no power in that region.
passages.original: מְהוֹדְעִ֤ין אֲנַ֙חְנָה֙ לְמַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֠י הֵ֣ן קִרְיְתָ֥א דָךְ֙ תִּתְבְּנֵ֔א וְשׁוּרַיָּ֖ה יִֽשְׁתַּכְלְל֑וּן לָקֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֔ה חֲלָק֙ בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֔א לָ֥א אִיתַ֖י לָֽךְ׃פ

passages.text: Then the king sent this reply: To Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of your associates living in Samaria and elsewhere in the region west of the Euphrates: Greetings.
passages.sermon:
The king sent a reply.
He addressed Rehum the commander.
He addressed Shimshai the scribe.
He addressed the rest of their associates.
These associates lived in Samaria.
Some associates lived in other places west of the Euphrates River.
The king greeted all of them.
passages.original: פִּתְגָמָ֞א שְׁלַ֣ח מַלְכָּ֗א עַל־ רְח֤וּם בְּעֵל־ טְעֵם֙ וְשִׁמְשַׁ֣י סָֽפְרָ֔א וּשְׁאָר֙ כְּנָוָ֣תְה֔וֹן דִּ֥י יָתְבִ֖ין בְּשָֽׁמְרָ֑יִן וּשְׁאָ֧ר עֲבַֽר־ נַהֲרָ֛ה שְׁלָ֖ם וּכְעֶֽת׃ס

passages.text: The letter you sent us has been translated and read in my presence.
passages.sermon:
The king received a letter from you.
The letter was translated.
Someone read the letter to me.
I heard the letter myself.
passages.original: נִשְׁתְּוָנָ֕א דִּ֥י שְׁלַחְתּ֖וּן עֲלֶ֑ינָא מְפָרַ֥שׁ קֱרִ֖י קָדָמָֽי׃

passages.text: I issued a decree, and a search was conducted. It was discovered that this city has revolted against kings from ancient times, engaging in rebellion and sedition.
passages.sermon:
The king gave an order.
Officials carried out a search.
They investigated the city of Jerusalem.
They found important information.
They discovered that Jerusalem has rebelled against kings for a long time.
The city has a history of rebellion.
People in Jerusalem have often caused trouble for rulers.
They have started uprisings and revolts in the past.
passages.original: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ וּבַקַּ֣רוּ וְהַשְׁכַּ֔חוּ דִּ֚י קִרְיְתָ֣א דָ֔ךְ מִן־ יוֹמָת֙ עָֽלְמָ֔א עַל־ מַלְכִ֖ין מִֽתְנַשְּׂאָ֑ה וּמְרַ֥ד וְאֶשְׁתַּדּ֖וּר מִתְעֲבֶד־ בַּֽהּ׃

passages.text: And mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem and exercised authority over the whole region west of the Euphrates; and tribute, duty, and toll were paid to them.
passages.sermon:
Mighty kings ruled over Jerusalem.
These kings had great power.
They controlled the whole region west of the Euphrates River.
People in that region paid tribute to these kings.
They also paid duty and toll to them.
passages.original: וּמַלְכִ֣ין תַּקִּיפִ֗ין הֲווֹ֙ עַל־ יְר֣וּשְׁלֶ֔ם וְשַׁ֨לִּיטִ֔ין בְּכֹ֖ל עֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה וּמִדָּ֥ה בְל֛וֹ וַהֲלָ֖ךְ מִתְיְהֵ֥ב לְהֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, issue an order for these men to stop, so that this city will not be rebuilt until I so order.
passages.sermon:
King Artaxerxes gave a command.
He told the officials to stop the men in Jerusalem.
He ordered them to halt the work immediately.
He said the city must not be rebuilt.
He said no one should build the city again until he gives a new order.
passages.original: כְּעַן֙ שִׂ֣ימוּ טְּעֵ֔ם לְבַטָּלָ֖א גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֑ךְ וְקִרְיְתָ֥א דָךְ֙ לָ֣א תִתְבְּנֵ֔א עַד־ מִנִּ֖י טַעְמָ֥א יִתְּשָֽׂם׃

passages.text: See that you do not neglect this matter. Why allow this threat to increase and the royal interests to suffer?
passages.sermon:
Pay careful attention to this matter.
Do not neglect it.
If you neglect it, the threat will grow.
If the threat grows, the king’s interests will suffer.
passages.original: וּזְהִירִ֥ין הֱו֛וֹ שָׁל֖וּ לְמֶעְבַּ֣ד עַל־ דְּנָ֑ה לְמָה֙ יִשְׂגֵּ֣א חֲבָלָ֔א לְהַנְזָקַ֖ת מַלְכִֽין׃ס

passages.text: When the text of the letter from King Artaxerxes was read to Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went immediately to the Jews in Jerusalem and forcibly stopped them.
passages.sermon:
King Artaxerxes was the ruler of Persia.
He sent a letter with an order.
People read the letter aloud.
Rehum heard the letter.
Shimshai the scribe also heard the letter.
Their associates listened too.
They all understood the king’s command.
They went at once to Jerusalem.
They went to the Jews living there.
They stopped the Jews from building.
They used force and power to make them stop.
passages.original: אֱדַ֗יִן מִן־ דִּ֞י פַּרְשֶׁ֤גֶן נִשְׁתְּוָנָא֙ דִּ֚י אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׂתָּא מַלְכָּ֔א קֱרִ֧י קֳדָם־ רְח֛וּם וְשִׁמְשַׁ֥י סָפְרָ֖א וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן אֲזַ֨לוּ בִבְהִיל֤וּ לִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ עַל־ יְה֣וּדָיֵ֔א וּבַטִּ֥לוּ הִמּ֖וֹ בְּאֶדְרָ֥ע וְחָֽיִל׃ס

passages.text: Thus the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
passages.sermon:
The house of God stood in Jerusalem.
People were building it.
They stopped the work.
The construction did not continue.
The work remained stopped.
This lasted until the second year of King Darius.
Darius was king of Persia.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֗יִן בְּטֵלַת֙ עֲבִידַ֣ת בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֔א דִּ֖י בִּירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וַהֲוָת֙ בָּֽטְלָ֔א עַ֚ד שְׁנַ֣ת תַּרְתֵּ֔ין לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־ פָּרָֽס׃פ
